Share of the embedded cells per label, with its spread across donors

Source: R/figures-mfi.R
composition_table.Rd

Each embedded cell carries ONE label, its most specific population (or its cluster), so the shares sum to 100. That is why the numbers differ from population_frequencies.csv, where the gates overlap – "CD3 pos" there includes the CD4 and CD8 T cells, and here it holds only the CD3+ cells no deeper population claimed. Under --subsample rare the cells carry a sampling_weight, and the shares are weighted back to the true composition.

Usage

composition_table(
  cells,
  label_col = "population_label",
  phenotype = NULL,
  group_col = NULL,
  colours = NULL,
  name_of = NULL,
  levels = NULL,
  marker_pct = NULL
)

Arguments

cells

Embedded cell table with sample_id and the label column.

label_col

Label column.

phenotype

Optional named character, label -> defining markers.

group_col

Optional study-group column in cells.

colours

Optional named character, label -> colour, carried into the table so a row can be matched to the figure.

name_of

Optional named character, label -> a second name (explore mode's matched subset).

levels

Optional label order. Every label in it gets a row, at 0% where absent, and rows keep this order – so the per-timepoint tables and figures list the cell types in the same order as the pooled one.

marker_pct

Optional numeric matrix, labels x markers, of the percent of each label positive for each marker; appended as pct_pos_<marker>.

Value

data.frame, largest share first and the catch-all last.
